lines.text: Somewhere right now, someone is typing, any update, for the fourth time this week.
You paid the deposit. The designer replied with a read receipt.
Flip it. You deliver the logo, and the client vanishes faster than free pizza.
The payment worked. The promise didn't.
Meet Kept. Money moves only when a promise is kept.
For freelancers. Plumbers. Suppliers. Anyone who has ever heard, I'll pay you Friday.
Just say the deal, the way you'd text it.
Pay the designer three hundred. A hundred now, two hundred when the logo lands. Refund me if nothing shows in a week.
Claude turns that into promises, and the exact rules that move the money.
Typing something shady, like a release fee to unlock your money? Kept flags the scam before anyone pays.
Then Kept does what no payment app does. It proves the deal.
Every delivery, every deadline, in every order they could happen. Sixty-three possible futures for one plumber visit, checked in two milliseconds.
And it caught a bug a tired lawyer would miss. Deliver on time, and the designer still loses two hundred dollars.
So the rules get repaired. Never your promises. Proved, across every outcome.
And before anyone pays a cent, you can see every way the deal can end.
You both approve the exact same terms. Same fingerprint. Read it out loud, like a secret handshake.
Then the money sits with PayPal. Not with a stranger. Not with us. Honestly, we don't want to hold it.
Under the hood, PayPal authorizes the full amount up front. Each release captures only its slice and pays it out. Refunds simply void the rest.
The logo lands. Maya taps accept.
Three hundred dollars, released exactly as proved. And Sam's phone lights up.
Kept's cut? Seven fifty. Only when money actually moves.
Same engine, different job. The plumber gets forty dollars for showing up, and the rest when the sink stops leaking. No show? Every cent comes home.
Every step is signed and hash-chained. Anyone can check the receipts in their own browser. No account, no trust required.
Now, the fun part. Let's cheat.
Change two hundred to two thousand. Bold. Also, broken.
Cover your tracks and re-hash it? Still broken. Only Kept's key can sign, and every later entry still points at the truth.
Not even we can rewrite it.
And before you pay anyone, paste their link. Look-alike sites get caught, right in your browser.
AI agents are about to spend real money for us. Someone has to make sure they spend it the way we meant.
Now give an AI agent a budget, not your card.
Paper? Paid. Toner? It asks you first. A sixty dollar chair? Denied. Nice try, robot.
A shop you never approved? Denied. A stolen token? Not today.
And every decision comes with a reason, in plain English.
Want stricter rules? Replay every real purchase first. At twenty dollars max, two of these would have been blocked.
Close the budget, and every unused dollar comes home.
Building agents? Kept speaks REST and MCP. One command, and your agent gets a budget it can't blow.
Or embed Kept in your own platform. One API key, a few calls, and every cent is accounted for.
Under the hood: Convex for the backend, PayPal for the money, Claude for the words, and a verifier that runs right in your browser.
Payments that keep their word. For people, and for the agents working for them.
Say it. Prove it. Hold it. Keep it.
Kept.
